title: About Homeschool Compass
description: Who we are, why this site exists, how we verify what a curriculum teaches, and how we make money — stated plainly.
bodyHtml:
Homeschool Compass is an independent guide for families teaching their children at home in the United States. We are not a curriculum publisher, we do not sell courses or co-op memberships, and we have no ownership relationship with any of the materials we cover. That independence is the entire point of the site.

Why this site exists

Most homeschool advice is written by someone with a product to move. That does not make it dishonest, but it makes it one-sided: a publisher has little reason to tell you that its course is wrong for a child who learns a different way, that a cheaper option teaches the same thing better, or that you already own what you need.

There is a second gap, and it is the one we care most about. Homeschool materials carry worldviews — some explicitly religious, some firmly secular, many unstated — and it is often genuinely hard to find out which before you have spent the money. A family looking for a Christian science course and a family looking for mainstream science are asking the same question: what does this book actually teach? Almost nobody answers it plainly for both.

What we do differently

We label what is inside the material, and we keep our own opinions out of it. For every curriculum we cover we report two separate facts and never merge them:

  • Content worldview — is there religious content in the material itself?
  • Publisher affiliation — is the company behind it religious?

Different families care about different ones of these. A publisher with Christian roots may produce a maths course with no religious content at all; for some readers that is irrelevant, for others it is decisive. By reporting both facts separately, we hand you the information rather than our verdict.

When a publisher makes no statement about worldview, we say unstated — which is not a synonym for neutral, and we do not treat it as one.

How we research

Worldview labels quote the publisher's own words and link to the page we took them from, with the month we last checked it. Legal requirements come from each state's published rules. Where we could not verify something at its source, we leave it out and say so, rather than filling the gap with a plausible guess.

We also state the limits of our checking. A label reflects a publisher's stated position and the samples they make public. We do not claim to have read every page of every course, because we have not, and a site that overstates what it verified is more dangerous than one that admits the boundary.

Who writes this

This is an early build, published under our editorial team rather than a personal byline. We compile and verify from primary sources instead of claiming homeschooling credentials or classroom experience we do not have. You will not find us writing in the voice of a homeschooling parent, or describing a curriculum as though we taught our own children with it. What we offer is careful, sourced compilation — and the receipts to check it.

How we make money

We plan to earn through advertising and through affiliate links to some materials we cover. A commission never changes a ranking or a verdict. When our conclusion is that something is not worth buying, it stays that way whether or not a commission is attached.

Corrections

Publishers revise their books and states change their rules, so some of what is here will go out of date. When we get something wrong we correct it, date the correction, and leave the record visible instead of quietly editing the page.{{^email}} A contact address for corrections will be published on our Contact page shortly.{{/email}}{{#email}} Corrections are welcome at {{email}}.{{/email}}

title: Contact
description: How to reach the Homeschool Compass editorial team, including for corrections.
bodyHtml:
{{^email}}

Homeschool Compass is newly launched, and our email address is being set up together with the site's domain. It will be published on this page as soon as it is live — we would rather leave this page honest than list an address that bounces.

{{/email}}{{#email}}

Write to us at {{email}}. One person reads everything that arrives, and we answer.

{{/email}}

Corrections come first

The message we most want to receive is a correction. If we have described what a curriculum teaches inaccurately, or summarised a state's requirements wrongly, tell us and point us at the source. We will check it against the publisher's or the state's own page, correct what is wrong, and date the correction on the article rather than editing it silently.

If something here disagrees with an official source, the official source is right and we are wrong. That is not politeness — it is how we would like you to use this site.

What we cannot help with

We are not able to give legal advice about your particular situation, assess a specific child, or tell you whether your records will satisfy a specific evaluator. Those questions belong with a qualified professional in your state, and we would be doing you a disservice by guessing at them.

Publishers

If you publish a curriculum we cover and believe our description of its content or worldview is inaccurate or out of date, we want to hear from you. Point us at the page on your own site that states your position and we will quote it directly.

title: Privacy Policy
description: What data this site collects, the cookies advertising partners may set, and how to control them.
bodyHtml:
This page explains what happens to data when you read Homeschool Compass. It is written to be understood rather than to be legally impressive.

What we collect ourselves

Homeschool Compass is a static website. We do not ask you to create an account, we do not run a newsletter sign-up, and we do not operate our own analytics or tracking scripts. We do not collect your name, your email address, or your children's information, because we never ask for them.

Server logs

Our hosting provider records standard technical information when a page is served — the request, the time, a general location derived from the network address, and the browser type. This is ordinary web server operation, used to keep the site available and to stop abuse. We do not use it to build a profile of you.

Advertising

We intend to display advertising on this site, including through Google AdSense. Advertising partners may set cookies or read existing ones in order to serve and measure ads, and in some cases to personalise them based on your previous visits to this and other websites.

Google's use of advertising cookies is described in Google's own advertising and privacy documentation. You can turn off personalised advertising in Google's Ads Settings, and you can manage or block cookies entirely in your browser's settings. Blocking advertising cookies does not stop you from reading anything here — the site works without them.

Depending on where you live, you may also see a consent notice before personalised advertising is enabled, and you can change or withdraw that choice at any time.

Affiliate links

Some links to curricula and other materials may be affiliate links. If you follow one and make a purchase, the retailer may pay us a commission at no additional cost to you, and may set a cookie to attribute that purchase. This never affects our recommendations or the order in which we rank anything.

Children

This site is written for parents and other adults who direct a child's education. It is not directed at children, and we do not knowingly collect information from them.

Your choices

You can block or delete cookies in your browser, use private browsing, or use an ad blocker. None of these will prevent you from reading the site.

Changes

If this policy changes in a way that affects you, we will update this page and the date below rather than change it silently.

Last updated: August 2026.{{^email}} A contact address for privacy questions will be published on our Contact page shortly.{{/email}}{{#email}} Questions about this policy: {{email}}.{{/email}}

title: Terms of Use
description: The terms you accept by using this site, including the limits of the educational and legal information published here.
bodyHtml:
By using Homeschool Compass you accept the terms below. They are deliberately short.

What this site is

Homeschool Compass publishes general information about homeschool curricula and about the rules that apply to homeschooling families in the United States. It is journalism and reference material, not professional advice.

This is not legal advice

Homeschool law is set by each state and changes. What we publish about a state's requirements is a summary of that state's published rules at the time we checked, and we say when we checked. It is not legal advice, it does not create any professional relationship, and it cannot account for your particular circumstances.

Before you rely on anything here to meet a legal obligation, confirm it against your state's own current published rules, and consult a qualified professional if your situation is contested or unusual. If what we publish disagrees with your state's official source, the official source is right and we are wrong — please tell us so we can correct it.

Accuracy and currency

We work from primary sources and date what we verify, but publishers revise their materials and states amend their rules. Information here may be out of date by the time you read it. We make no warranty that the site is complete, current, or error-free.

Curriculum descriptions

Our descriptions of what a curriculum teaches, including any worldview label, reflect the publisher's stated position and the samples they make public at the time of checking. They are our good-faith reading of that material and are not endorsed by, or affiliated with, the publishers. Trade names and product names belong to their respective owners and are used here for identification and comment.

Affiliate relationships

Some outbound links may earn us a commission. This is disclosed in our editorial policy and never affects a ranking or a verdict.

Your use of the site

You may read, share, and quote from this site with attribution and a link. You may not republish substantial portions as your own, or scrape the site to build a competing database.

Third-party links

We link to publishers, state agencies and other outside sites. We do not control them and are not responsible for their content, their accuracy, or their privacy practices.

Limitation of liability

To the fullest extent permitted by law, we are not liable for any loss arising from your use of, or reliance on, this site. Decisions about your child's education — and about complying with your state's requirements — are yours.

Changes

We may update these terms; the current version always appears on this page.
